IDF personnel arrived on scene, spoke with settlers, and moved a car to block the road. Khanna has directly accused the IDF of siding with the settlers, calling it a 'huge mistake.' He stated he is 'strongly considering' a presidential run and said the trip made him more resolved to do so. The incident is part of a pattern of Democratic presidential aspirants visiting the region to establish critic credentials. Separately, Qatar's sovereign wealth fund has vetoed a Volkswagen joint venture with an Israeli firm that would have produced vehicles supporting Israel's Iron Dome mobile air-defense system, threatening hundreds of jobs at a VW site. In Gaza, Israeli attacks have killed at least 1,098 Palestinians since the US-brokered ceasefire in October, including five in the latest strikes — among them a 9-year-old girl. Kamal Adwan hospital was struck by an Israeli drone, wounding health workers; power cuts are plunging Gaza hospitals into darkness. Nine months into the ceasefire, Israel now controls nearly 70% of Gaza, up from roughly 50% at ceasefire onset. The US has sent a team to Beirut to shore up the Israel-Hizbollah ceasefire, while Lebanon's president is calling for international pressure on Israel to begin withdrawing its forces.

items.title: EU says ‘addictive’ features on Instagram and Facebook breach its rules

clusters.state_of_play: Meta launched an AI image generation tool called Muse on Tuesday that allows Instagram users to tag public profiles and generate AI images using faces from those accounts' posts. Public Instagram users are not notified when their posts are used. Following widespread backlash over privacy and consent — including criticism from a Hollywood union — Meta has discontinued the Muse Image feature, saying it 'misses the mark' on users' privacy. Separately, the European Commission on Friday issued a preliminary charge sheet finding Meta in breach of the EU's Digital Services Act over 'addictive' design features on Instagram and Facebook — specifically video autoplay and infinite scroll — which regulators say cause compulsive use and harm users' physical and mental health. Meta faces a fine of up to 6% of global turnover. Additionally, Meta is appealing a landmark Los Angeles jury verdict that found it liable for social media addiction among young users.

clusters.title: Meta Verified scam threatens Facebook deletion

items.title: Meta Verified scam threatens Facebook deletion

clusters.state_of_play: Meta launched an AI image generation tool called Muse on Tuesday that allows Instagram users to tag public profiles and generate AI images using faces from those accounts' posts. Public Instagram users are not notified when their posts are used. Following widespread backlash over privacy and consent — including criticism from a Hollywood union — Meta has discontinued the Muse Image feature, saying it 'misses the mark' on users' privacy. Separately, the European Commission on Friday issued a preliminary charge sheet finding Meta in breach of the EU's Digital Services Act over 'addictive' design features on Instagram and Facebook — specifically video autoplay and infinite scroll — which regulators say cause compulsive use and harm users' physical and mental health. Meta faces a fine of up to 6% of global turnover. Additionally, Meta is appealing a landmark Los Angeles jury verdict that found it liable for social media addiction among young users.

clusters.state_of_play: DR Congo is experiencing its fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, with nearly 1,800 confirmed cases and over 600 deaths. Two U.S. citizens have tested positive — an American doctor earlier in the outbreak (transferred to Germany for treatment) and a second U.S. citizen working for a humanitarian organization. The CDC is coordinating with the person's employer and Congolese partners to prevent further transmission. New suspected cases have emerged in parts of Congo previously unaffected, signaling spread beyond the Ituri epicenter. Containment efforts are further threatened by health workers protesting non-payment. In a parallel development, the first patients have been enrolled in a clinical treatment trial in the Ituri region — set up in just six weeks after the outbreak was declared, a record pace — testing two drugs with hopes of reducing mortality rates. There is currently no approved drug for this Ebola outbreak.
